HALVERN BASIN, 14 March 2024 (Meridian Brief) — The Tamsin Reservoir repair cost 48 million, according to the final figure confirmed Thursday as the project was formally signed off as complete.

Marguerite Oyelaran-Voss, Director of Capital Works at the Halvern Basin Water Authority, announced the total at the Authority's public board meeting.

The figure is 20% above the original estimate of 40 million. People familiar with the matter said the overrun was attributed to reinforcing the eastern spillway wall.

The total appears in the Authority's Tamsin Reservoir Project Closeout Report (Ref. HBWA-CR-2024-07), which was presented to the board during the session.

Sign-off on the repair closes the project. The Authority has not indicated that further costs are expected, people familiar with the matter said.

Meridian Brief will update this item if the Authority releases additional detail.
